props.gloss_en: the mishna (81b): one who slaughters [mother and offspring] with an unfit slaughter -- R' Shimon exempts
R' Meir: one who slaughters mother and offspring with an unfit slaughter is liable (taught in the mishna in the Sages' name, per R' Yochanan)
the mishna (85a.7): one who slaughters an undomesticated animal or bird with an unfit slaughter -- R' Meir obligates covering the blood
R' Shimon: an unfit slaughter does not obligate covering the blood (taught in the mishna in the Sages' name, per R' Yochanan)
Rebbi saw R' Meir's words on oto ve'et beno and taught them in the language of the Sages
and R' Shimon's [words] on covering the blood, and taught them in the language of the Sages
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: R' Meir derives 'shechita / shechita' from offerings slaughtered outside: as there an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so here
R' Mani bar Pattish: R' Shimon derives from 'slaughter and prepare' (Gen 43:16): as there a fit slaughter, so here a fit slaughter
R' Meir: does oto ve'et beno not apply to sacrificial animals?
the school of R' Yishmael: 'and the priest shall return' (Lev 14:39), 'and the priest shall come' (Lev 14:44) -- returning and coming are one [for a gezera shava]
Reish Lakish: R' Meir derives 'shefika / shefika' (Lev 17:13; 17:4) from offerings slaughtered outside: as there an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so here
R' Shimon: 'that may be eaten' (Lev 17:13) is written
R' Meir: that [phrase] comes to exclude an impure bird
R' Shimon: why is an impure bird [excluded]? because it is not edible -- a tereifa too is not edible
not for everything did R' Meir say an unfit slaughter is called slaughter: R' Meir concedes that it does not permit [the animal] for eating
and not for everything did R' Shimon say an unfit slaughter is not called slaughter: R' Shimon concedes that it purifies [the animal] from nevela impurity

first answer: [R' Meir's concession] is needed for one who slaughters a tereifa and finds in it a live nine-month fetus -- one might say, since R' Meir holds an unfit slaughter is slaughter, the mother's slaughter serves the fetus and it needs no slaughter of its own
R' Meir: a ben pekua requires slaughter
the Rabbis: its mother's slaughter purifies it [the ben pekua]
Rebbi holds like R' Meir, who says an unfit slaughter is called slaughter
and holds like the Rabbis, who say its mother's slaughter purifies it

second answer: [the concession] is needed for Rebbi's view -- since the Rabbis say the mother's slaughter purifies it, one might say the [tereifa] mother's slaughter serves [the fetus] and it needs no slaughter; this teaches us otherwise
'and if there die of the animals' (Lev 11:39): some animals defile and some do not -- which? a tereifa that one slaughtered
one who slaughters a tereifa, or slaughters and it is found a tereifa, both chullin in the courtyard -- R' Shimon permits benefit
and the Sages forbid [benefit]
what the concession teaches: even for R' Shimon, who permits benefit from a tereifa slaughtered as chullin in the courtyard, its slaughter purifies it from nevela impurity
R' Shimon holds [the prohibition of] chullin [slaughtered] in the courtyard is Torah law
R' Shimon: chullin slaughtered in the courtyard shall be burned in fire
and likewise an undomesticated animal slaughtered in the courtyard
granted if it is Torah law: that is why we decree on the undomesticated animal because of the domesticated one
(entertained) but if you say [the prohibition] is rabbinic
(within the hypothesis) the domesticated animal's reason is lest one come to eat kodashim outside -- it is itself a decree
and shall we arise and decree a decree upon a decree?
moths infested R' Chiyya's flax; he came before Rebbi
Rebbi to him: take a bird and slaughter it over the tub of water -- [the moths] smell the blood and leave it
one who slaughters and needs the blood must cover it; how should he act? either stab it or uproot [the simanim]
Rav Dimi: [Rebbi] said to him: go, make it a tereifa
Ravin: [Rebbi] said to him: go, stab [it]
(entertained) and if you say [Rebbi] holds there is no Torah slaughter for a bird, and its stabbing is its slaughter
Rebbi: 'as I have commanded you' (Deut 12:21) teaches that Moses was commanded on the gullet and the windpipe, on the majority of one in a bird and the majority of two in an animal
(entertained) and if you say [Rebbi] holds an unfit slaughter is called slaughter [and obligates covering]
from when the exiles came up, meteors, earthquakes, storm winds and thunder ceased, their wine did not sour and their flax was not stricken; and the Sages set their eyes on R' Chiyya and his sons
when their merit avails, it avails the world, not themselves
Rav: each and every day a bat kol emerges and says: the whole world is fed for the sake of Chanina my son, and for Chanina my son a kav of carobs suffices from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve

grounds.gloss_en: ורבי מאיר נמי ליגמר מטבוח? -- let R' Meir too learn from 'tevoach' [that only a fit slaughter counts]

answered_by.gloss_en: דנין שחיטה משחיטה ואין דנין שחיטה מטביחה -- one learns shechita from shechita, not shechita from tevicha

schemas.gloss_en: per R' Mani bar Pattish: from 'slaughter and prepare' (Gen 43:16) -- as there a fit slaughter, so with oto ve'et beno only a fit slaughter

grounds.gloss_en: ורבי שמעון נמי ליגמר משחוטי חוץ? -- let R' Shimon too learn from offerings slaughtered outside

answered_by.gloss_en: דנין חולין מחולין ואין דנין חולין מקדשים -- one learns chullin from chullin, not chullin from kodashim

schemas.gloss_en: per Reish Lakish: 'and he shall pour out' (Lev 17:13) / 'he has poured blood' (Lev 17:4) -- as with offerings slaughtered outside an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so with covering the blood

grounds.gloss_en: ורבי שמעון: אשר יאכל כתיב -- 'that may be eaten': only a slaughter that renders it edible

attacked_by.gloss_en: ורבי מאיר: ההוא למעוטי עוף טמא הוא דאתא -- that phrase is spent excluding an impure bird

answered_by.gloss_en: ורבי שמעון: עוף טמא מאי טעמא -- דלאו בר אכילה הוא; טרפה נמי לאו בר אכילה הוא -- the impure bird is excluded for being inedible, and a tereifa is inedible too

supports.gloss_en: היינו דקאמר רבי חייא: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי מאיר באותו ואת בנו -- R' Meir's rejoinder is what R' Chiyya [bar Abba] referred to
והיינו דאמר רבי חייא: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי שמעון בכסוי הדם -- R' Shimon's last word is what R' Chiyya [bar Abba] referred to
דרבי סבר לה כרבי מאיר ... וסבר לה כרבנן דאמרי שחיטת אמו מטהרתו

אין, והתנן רבי שמעון אומר: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה ישרפו באש, וכן חיה -- the chaya ruling is explicable only as a decree because of a Torah prohibition (kind svara: no support kind for a בשלמא-argument from a mishna)
כדרב יהודה אמר רב: כל העולם כולו ניזון בשביל חנינא בני, וחנינא בני די לו בקב חרובין -- merit that feeds the world while its owner lacks

objections.gloss_en: ותסברא? והאמר רבי מאיר: בן פקועה טעון שחיטה -- for R' Meir even a fetus of a properly slaughtered mother needs its own slaughter, so the case teaches nothing on his view (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)
היכי עביד הכי? והתניא: השוחט וצריך לדם חייב לכסות -- one who slaughters for the blood must still cover it; he should stab or uproot instead

answered_by.gloss_en: כי אתא רב דימי אמר: צא טרוף אמר ליה -- Rebbi told him to make it a tereifa first (= p_tze_trof)
כי אתא רבין אמר: צא נחור אמר ליה -- Rebbi told him to stab it (= p_tze_nechor)

objections.gloss_en: והתניא רבי אומר: כאשר צויתך -- Rebbi himself derives that a bird's slaughter is from the Torah
והא אמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי שמעון בכסוי הדם -- Rebbi follows R' Shimon on covering the blood (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)
ומי נפל ליה יאניבא בכיתניה? והאמר רבין בר אבא ... ולא לקה פשתנם, ונתנו חכמים עיניהם ברבי חייא ובניו (kind svara: no objection kind for והאמר)

answered_by.gloss_en: כי מהניא זכותייהו -- אעלמא, אדידהו -- לא (= p_zchut_leolam_lo_ledidhu)
